hero.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained, more expected this summer
hero.teaser: Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike, both now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.
hero.body:
Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike. Both are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service, which warns that conditions fueling these fires will persist throughout the summer months.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said this is peak season for brush fires in the region. The summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them highly receptive when lightning strikes occur. However, Grubitch emphasized that residents should not be alarmed by these conditions, as they are typical for this time of year. He explained that while rain often extinguishes fires immediately after they start, some fires can travel underground and resurface days later, making them more difficult to detect and contain.

The Florida Forest Service is relying on public assistance to help monitor and respond to brush fires quickly. Grubitch stressed that residents play a crucial role in helping the department do its job effectively. He urged people to never assume someone else has already reported a brush fire they spot, emphasizing the importance of immediate notification. According to Grubitch, if residents see something, they should say something, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control.

With summer conditions expected to continue creating favorable environments for brush fires, the Florida Forest Service will maintain its heightened monitoring and response efforts throughout the season. The department continues to track contained fires and remains prepared to respond to new incidents as they arise. Residents are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any signs of smoke or fire to local authorities immediately, regardless of whether they believe others may have already called it in. Quick reporting remains one of the most effective tools in preventing small fires from becoming larger, more dangerous blazes that threaten homes and natural areas.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Cardinals even series with St. Lucie Mets, decisive game three set for Sunday
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach Cardinals defeated the St.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Cardinals defeated the St. Lucie Mets on Saturday to even their playoff series at one game apiece. Palm Beach built an early lead and held off a late rally by St. Lucie to force a decisive third game.

The Cardinals controlled much of the contest after jumping ahead early. St. Lucie mounted a late comeback attempt but could not complete the rally, allowing Palm Beach to tie the series.

The series finale is scheduled for Sunday. The winner will advance in the playoffs while the loser's season will end.

The St. Lucie Mets play their home games at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. The decisive game three will determine which team moves forward in the postseason.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District terminates 3 firefighters after hazing investigation involving electric shocks
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District released investigative reports Saturday detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. District administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024.

The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally. Attorney J.K. Keller of Allen, Norton & Blue concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others.

The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees. The media advisory also includes a separate 2025 workplace culture assessment by attorney Susan Gainey, who found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing that blurred the line between camaraderie and misconduct. Although that earlier investigation did not substantiate harassment claims, Gainey recommended reassigning personnel and implementing additional leadership and workplace culture training.

The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process. "As the disciplined individuals have since exercised their rights to initiate the formal contractual grievance and arbitration process, the District will confidently present these documented facts within that legal forum and will have no further public comment at this time," the district said.

cards.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon at Sebastian as severe weather batters Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: Video sent to WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showed a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. Severe weather stretched from Sebastian to Port St. Lucie and into Okeechobee County.
cards.body:
Video sent to the WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showed a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. In Port St. Lucie, WPTV weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. Moore O'Rourke said it got black, the wind started raging and the sky had lit up like she had not seen.

Severe weather stretched to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Port St. Lucie also saw significant lightning activity. St. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. At the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue, fire crews responded to an evening house fire. At the time of the storm, WPTV radar picked up a significant amount of lightning in the area. St. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate. Moore O'Rourke said the storm was radical and a little scary.

cards.headline: E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks prompt Treasure Coast residents to avoid lettuce
cards.teaser: Confirmed cases of cyclospora have been reported in St. Lucie and Martin counties as contaminated produce linked to Taco Bell locations spreads concern across South Florida.
cards.body:
Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected by E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks linked to contaminated lettuce, with confirmed cases also reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast. According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: 2 in St. Lucie County and 1 in Martin County.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers. Barone recommends foods like bananas, melons and avocados, and says beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein. She warns against bagged lettuce and recommends buying whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers and avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly.

Barone recommends cleaning produce using a 1-to-3 part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water. Then soak, massage and clean off your produce and make sure to cook your vegetables. George Lorenz said he is taking precautions while grabbing lunch in downtown West Palm Beach. Hendriette Peckens in Boynton Beach said she bought oranges, bread and apples and is avoiding produce because of the outbreak.

cards.headline: Josh Kerr breaks 27-year-old mile world record with 3:42.66 in London
cards.teaser: Great Britain's Josh Kerr shattered the mile world record Saturday, running 3:42.66 to break Hicham El Guerrouj's mark of 3:43.13 that had stood since 1999.
cards.body:
Great Britain's Josh Kerr shattered one of track and field's most enduring records Saturday, running the mile in 3:42.66 at a Diamond League event in London. The performance broke Hicham El Guerrouj's previous world record of 3:43.13, which had stood since 1999. Kerr made no secret of his intentions leading up to the race, revealing earlier in the week that he had run 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor Brooks called the effort "Project 222," a reference to the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. The shoe company announced Friday that this was the moment Kerr stood to make history and bring the mile record home.

The 27-year-old has established himself as one of the world's premier middle-distance runners in recent years. He won bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and followed that with a silver medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr competed at the University of New Mexico, where he captured multiple NCAA titles and set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018.

Kerr's achievement stands in contrast to other recent high-profile distance record attempts that were not officially recognized. Kenyan marathon star Eliud Kipchoge became the first person to run a marathon in under 2 hours in 2019, but the performance was not eligible for world record status because it was not conducted under standard race conditions. Similarly, Kenyan runner Faith Kipyegon attempted to become the first woman to run a sub-4-minute mile but fell short. Her time of 4:06.42 would have broken the women's world record had it been set during an official competition.

Kerr's record-setting performance came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events, giving it official status. American Yared Nuguse finished second in Saturday's race with a time of 3:45.69. The successful record attempt caps years of development for Kerr, who has steadily progressed through collegiate athletics and onto the world stage, culminating in his history-making run in London.

cards.headline: Cardinals Homer Twice, Defeat St. Lucie Mets 7-4
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The loss evened
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The loss evened the three-game series at one game apiece and set up a rubber match Sunday afternoon.

Palm Beach opened the scoring with three runs in the bottom of the first inning. Brayden Smith singled to center field, and an error by D'Andre Smith allowed the Cardinals to capitalize. Ryan Weingartner and Sebastian Dos Santos scored on the play before Brayden Smith came around to give Palm Beach a 3-0 advantage.

St. Lucie responded with two runs in the second inning.

Chase Meggers delivered an RBI single with runners on the corners, scoring AJ Salgado. Jeremy Rodriguez then brought Simon Juan home on a fielder's choice to cut the Cardinals' lead to 3-2.

Palm Beach began pulling away in the fourth inning. Alex Birg drove in Yordalin Pena with an RBI single before Dos Santos launched a two-run home run. The Cardinals eventually built a 7-2 lead.

The Mets bullpen settled the game down after Joe Scarborough entered from the bullpen. Scarborough delivered two scoreless and hitless innings while striking out four batters.

It marked Scarborough's second consecutive scoreless appearance at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Antonio Jimenez gave the Mets another run in the top of the sixth inning with a solo home run. It was Jimenez's sixth homer of the season and his fourth during July, cutting the Palm Beach lead to 7-3.

Caden Wooster followed Scarborough with another strong relief appearance. Wooster allowed just one hit over two scoreless innings and struck out four.

Scarborough and Wooster combined to strike out eight batters over four shutout innings. St. Lucie's pitching staff finished the game with 12 strikeouts, reaching double digits for the second consecutive night.

The Mets mounted one final rally in the ninth inning and brought the potential tying run to the plate. Palm Beach reliever Nathan Shinn escaped the threat and secured the victory for the Cardinals.

St. Lucie fell to 7-14 in the second half and 40-47 overall. Palm Beach improved to 13-9 in the second half and 65-42 overall.

The teams will decide the series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 12:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Residents Report Five Cyclospora Cases Since May
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Health has confirmed five cases of cyclospora in the Treasure Coast region since May amid nationwide produce contamination outbreaks.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County. The cases are part of nationwide outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora linked to contaminated produce, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, causing many South Florida residents to change their eating habits and avoid leafy greens altogether.

Families across the region are steering clear of salads and contaminated produce that can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are avoiding lettuce and similar foods. Jenny Rhodes said she misses her salads and berries but believes it is better to be careful. In West Palm Beach, George Lorenz said he has heard about the outbreak and is staying away from affected produce. In Boynton Beach, shopper Hendriette Peckens said she bought oranges, apples and bread instead of greens and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said the outbreaks are not an excuse to abandon healthy eating. She recommended consumers focus on produce with protective outer layers, suggesting they stick to melon and foods with harder skin that can be peeled, including bananas, melons and avocados. However, she warned that people still need to wash these items before cutting into them and peeling them. Barone also said beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein.

Barone's biggest warning was to avoid bagged lettuce if possible. She recommended buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers. She also warned that berries, especially raspberries, are difficult to clean properly and should be avoided. Barone recommended cleaning produce using a 1 to 3 part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water. Consumers should soak, massage and clean off produce and make sure to cook vegetables. She emphasized that washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them is essential, and consumers should wash items with harder skins before cutting into them.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said that route is performing well. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said. As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

cards.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bobby Portis join Miami Heat with championship goals
cards.teaser: The Miami Heat introduced Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis Jr. at the Kaseya Center on Thursday, with both players receiving standing ovations from fans.
cards.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis Jr. were introduced as Miami Heat players Thursday afternoon at the Kaseya Center, where loud chants of "Giannis" filled the arena. Head Coach Erik Spoelstra said Pat Riley asked him if he wanted to coach Antetokounmpo, and he said yes to coaching the two-time MVP, NBA champion and Finals MVP. Antetokounmpo, who is coming off back-to-back injury-filled seasons, said he thrives on pressure and needs it at this point in his career to go to the next level. The 6'11, 240-pound forward said he is not at Miami to talk about measurables but to discuss how many championships he can help bring. Antetokounmpo said he feels like whenever he puts his mind to something, he usually accomplishes it, and this is the best route for him to do that.

Portis said he prides himself on working every day in the summer to get better and has been coming off the bench his whole career as a sixth man type of guy. Portis said he has been playing with Antetokounmpo for six years now, going on seven, and his relationship with Bam Adebayo has been built off being competitors. Spoelstra said the squad with Antetokounmpo, Portis and Adebayo will play a lot of positionless ball. Antetokounmpo said the moment he is coached hard, everyone else is going to follow, adding he does not want it sugar-coated and needs the truth so he can apply that to the game.

cards.headline: Florida Panthers to open 2026-27 season on road before home opener October 11
cards.teaser: The Panthers will begin their regular season against the 2026 Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes on September 29 before returning to Amerant Bank Arena for their home opener.
cards.body:
The Florida Panthers will begin their 2026-27 NHL regular season on the road, taking on four Western Conference opponents. The Panthers will open against the 2026 Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes on September 29, marking a marquee matchup to begin the year. The road trip continues with a stop in San Jose on October 6.

After their four-game road swing, the Panthers will return to South Florida for their home opener on Saturday, October 11, when they welcome the Minnesota Wild to Amerant Bank Arena. December will be particularly busy with seven home games, including four special holiday matchups to close out 2026. The Panthers play the Buffalo Sabres in December as part of the holiday schedule. Fans will enjoy two consecutive five-game homestands during the season, with the first running December 19-30 and the second from March 2-12.

cards.headline: World Cup Final security ramped up for Sunday's Argentina-Spain match in New Jersey
cards.teaser: The World Cup Final has been designated a Level 1 Special Event with enhanced security measures including a Secret Service perimeter for President Trump's attendance.
cards.body:
A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there's anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: World Cup Final tickets start at $7,700 as demand drives prices to record levels
cards.teaser: The cheapest ticket for Sunday's World Cup Final in New Jersey costs about $7,700 on resale sites, nearly identical to what the median U.S. household earns in an entire month.
cards.body:
The cheapest ticket on resale sites currently for sale for Sunday's World Cup final is about $7,700. That's nearly identical to what the median U.S. household earns in an entire month. If you want to sit in the lower bowl of the stadium, be prepared to spend at least $10,000.

FIFA has faced criticism over the high ticket prices, which it says reflect strong global demand. Tickets for the third-place game in Miami start at about $700. According to Forbes, this year's World Cup Final could end up being the most expensive sports ticket in U.S. history.

cards.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPad use to prevent artificial intelligence from making game decisions
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday night to prevent tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make in-game decisions.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

hero.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
hero.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
Families looking for ways to give back this summer can take part in the TLC Program at B'nai Torah Congregation, where volunteers help with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. The program, led by Summer Faerman, is part of B'nai Torah Congregation's broader effort to connect people of all ages with mitzvah opportunities or meaningful good deeds. Organizers say the TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed and has helped make service a central part of synagogue life since 2012.

B'nai Torah Congregation describes the TLC Program as a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. The congregation says the program focuses on hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations, special needs and other community concerns. Participants can volunteer in a variety of ways, including making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology.

Organizers say the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation. The goal is to show service as something practical, welcoming and easy to begin. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need.

As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

He urged people to never assume someone else has already reported a brush fire they spot, emphasizing the importance of immediate notification. According to Grubitch, if residents see something, they should say something, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control.

With summer conditions expected to continue creating favorable environments for brush fires, the Florida Forest Service will maintain its heightened monitoring and response efforts throughout the season. The department continues to track contained fires and remains prepared to respond to new incidents as they arise. Residents are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any signs of smoke or fire to local authorities immediately, regardless of whether they believe others may have already called it in. Quick reporting remains one of the most effective tools in preventing small fires from becoming larger, more dangerous blazes that threaten homes and natural areas.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District terminates 3 firefighters after hazing investigation involving electric shocks
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. According to the district, administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024.

The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally. Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others.

The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees.

The media advisory also includes a separate 2025 workplace culture assessment by attorney Susan Gainey, who found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing that blurred the line between camaraderie and misconduct. Although that earlier investigation did not substantiate harassment claims, Gainey recommended reassigning personnel and implementing additional leadership and workplace culture training. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process. The district said it will confidently present these documented facts within that legal forum and will have no further public comment at this time.

hero.headline: Waterspouts, Lightning Strikes and Fires Hit Sebastian and Port St. Lucie During Friday Severe Weather
hero.body:
Friday's severe weather left a trail of impacts across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showed a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. The dramatic weather event was captured by several residents as the system moved through the area.

In Port St. Lucie, WPTV weather spotters recorded video of heavy rain moving through the region. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge measured over 3 inches of rainfall. She described the sudden intensity of the storm, saying the sky turned black and the wind started raging. Moore O'Rourke said the lightning lit up the sky in a way she had not seen before.

The severe weather extended all the way to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Port St. Lucie experienced significant lightning activity throughout the storm. The Lucie County Fire District reported that crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after receiving reports that a lightning strike had ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening hours. Radar data showed a significant amount of lightning in the area at the time of the fire. However, the Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause of the house fire, as the fire marshal's office still needs to complete its investigation.

Moore O'Rourke summed up what many residents across the region experienced as the storms passed through the area. She described the weather event as radical and said it was a little scary. From waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires, Friday's severe weather served as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power across the Treasure Coast.

cards.headline: JetBlue Cancels Vero Beach to New York Route Less Than a Year After Launch
cards.teaser: JetBlue has discontinued its flight service between Vero Beach and New York less than a year after launching the route.
cards.body:
JetBlue has pulled the plug on its New York to Florida Vero Beach route less than a year after launch. The cancellation raises fresh questions over US regional air travel demand and Treasure Coast tourism connectivity.

The airline's decision to end the route comes after a brief period of service connecting Vero Beach to the New York area. The discontinuation affects travelers who used the direct flight option between the Treasure Coast and the Northeast.
